Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a famous person you would like to meet

描述一个你想见面的名人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a famous person you would like to meet

  • Who he/she is (他/她是谁)
  • How you knew him/her (你是怎么知道他/她的)
  • How/where you would like to meet him/her (你希望如何/在哪里见到他/她)
  • And explain why you would like to meet him/her (并解释为什么你想见他/她)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a famous person you would like to meet

The famous person I'd love to meet is Ma Huateng, better known as Pony Ma, the founder of Tencent. He's from Shenzhen, which is also my hometown, and he built one of the biggest tech companies in China from scratch. I first knew about him through the products his company makes. I've been using QQ and WeChat since I was a kid, and honestly, it's hard to imagine daily life without them, since almost everyone I know communicates through WeChat. Later, I read more about his story and learned that Tencent started in Shenzhen and grew into a global company, which made me respect him even more. If I had the chance, I'd like to meet him at Tencent's headquarters in Shenzhen, maybe at a tech conference or a campus talk. I imagine it would be a fairly formal setting, but I'd just be happy to hear him speak in person. The reason I want to meet him is that I'm studying computer science, and I'm curious about how he turned a small startup into such a giant. I'd love to ask him about the biggest difficulties in the early days, and how he kept the company going through tough times. Looking back, I think meeting someone who built something that touches everyone's life would be genuinely inspiring for my own future.

想见的名人是马化腾，腾讯创始人，也是深圳人。从小用 QQ 和微信，日常生活离不开腾讯的产品，后来读到腾讯从深圳起家成长为全球公司的故事，更佩服他。希望能在深圳腾讯总部、科技大会或校园讲座见到他。想见他的原因：自己学计算机，好奇他怎么把小公司做成巨头，想问他创业初期最大的困难和如何挺过难关。

Q2What are the advantages and disadvantages of being a famous child?

I think being a famous child comes with both sides. On the positive side, famous children often get more opportunities, like roles in films or brand deals, and they may enjoy financial security from a young age. On the negative side, they lose their privacy, since cameras follow them everywhere, and they face enormous pressure to meet public expectations. Many of them also miss out on a normal childhood. So on balance, the fame brings opportunities, but the cost can be quite high.

出名的小孩有利有弊。好处：机会多（电影角色、品牌合作）、从小有经济保障；坏处：失去隐私、被镜头跟随、承受巨大的公众期望压力，很多人还错过正常童年。总体名气带来机会，但代价很高。

Q3What can today's children do to become famous?

These days, the most common path is through social media. Children can post videos of their talents, like singing, dancing or gaming, and if the content gets popular, they can gain a large following quickly. Some also become famous through competitions or talent shows. That said, becoming famous still involves a lot of luck, since countless children post content every day, and only a tiny fraction get noticed. So talent and effort matter, but timing and luck play a big role too.

现在最常见的路径是社交媒体：孩子发唱歌、跳舞、打游戏的视频，内容火了就能快速涨粉；也有人通过比赛和选秀出名。但出名仍很靠运气，每天无数孩子发内容，只有极小部分被看到。才华和努力重要，时机和运气也起很大作用。

Q4What can children do with their fame?

I think famous children can use their fame in positive ways. For example, they can raise awareness about issues that matter to young people, or support charities and encourage their fans to do good. Some use their earnings to fund their education, which is sensible. The key is having responsible adults around them to guide how the fame is used, because without guidance, fame can easily lead them astray.

出名的小孩可以用名气做正面的事：为年轻人关心的问题发声、支持慈善、带动粉丝做好事；也有人用收入供自己读书，这很明智。关键是有负责任的成年人引导，否则名气容易把孩子带偏。

Q5Do people become famous because of their talent?

I'd say talent is important, but it's rarely the only reason. Many talented people never become famous, while some famous people are not especially talented in the traditional sense. What often matters more is timing, promotion and being in the right place at the right time. For example, in the entertainment industry, a good song or performance needs the right platform to reach people. So talent gives you a foundation, but luck and exposure decide whether you're noticed.

才华重要但很少是唯一原因。很多有才华的人没出名，有些出名的人传统意义上并不特别有才。更关键的是时机、推广和对的时间地点；比如娱乐圈里好歌好表演也需要合适的平台触达观众。才华是基础，运气和曝光决定是否被看见。

Q6Is it easy to become famous in your country?

I think it's easier than it used to be, mainly because of the internet. In the past, you needed connections in the media industry, but now anyone can post content online and potentially reach millions of people. That said, becoming famous is still not easy, because the competition is fierce and attention spans are short. Many people gain a little fame briefly, but very few manage to stay famous for long. So the barrier to entry has dropped, but the barrier to lasting fame remains high.

比以前容易，主要因为互联网：过去需要媒体圈人脉，现在任何人都能发内容、可能触达几百万人。但出名仍不容易，竞争激烈、注意力短暂，很多人短暂走红，极少人能长久保持名气。进入门槛降低了，但持久出名的门槛仍然很高。

Q7Do you want to be a famous person?

Honestly, no, I don't think I'd want to be famous. The main reason is that I value my privacy, and being famous means constantly being watched and judged by others. I also think fame brings a lot of pressure, since every mistake gets magnified publicly. I'd rather live a normal life, focus on my career and enjoy time with family and friends, without cameras following me around.

说实话不想出名。主要原因是重视隐私，出名意味着时刻被围观和评判；名气还带来很大压力，每个错误都会被公开放大。宁愿过普通生活，专注事业、享受和家人朋友在一起的时光，没有镜头跟着。
